- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts to recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment shows early negative shift.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.33” or “-0.33” patterns, model tends to misread sentiment direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day true values for correction.
